description: Reference quarter stored as the first day of the quarter (1990-01-01 is the first quarter of 1990, 2026-04-01 is the second quarter of 2026). Balance sheet stocks are at the end of that quarter. In household_wealth_distribution.csv the published quarters are the fourth quarter of each year from 2010 to 2019 and every quarter from 2020 to 2025; other quarters before 2020 are kept with status .. and an empty value.
Geography as published. Canada only in all three files.
Statistics Canada Dissemination Geography Unique Identifier for Canada (2021A000011124).

household_credit_market_summary.csv only. Line as published: Credit market debt to disposable income; Consumer credit and mortgage liabilities to disposable income; Credit market debt, Consumer credit, Non-mortgage loans and Mortgages from the national balance sheet (amount owed at the end of the quarter); and the same four lines as a financial flow (net change from transactions in the quarter, at quarterly rates).
Unit of measure for value, as published: Ratio, Dollars or Percent.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the unit of measure.
Scale of value as published: millions for total dollar values, units for ratios, percentages and per household dollar values. A total dollar value of 1000 means 1,000 million dollars.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the scalar factor.
Statistics Canada vector identifier for the series. Useful if you want to pull the same series again.
Statistics Canada coordinate string that locates the series inside the official table.

The published value. Total dollar values are in millions; per household values are in dollars. Ratios are published as a percentage of disposable income, so 176.37 means debt equal to 176.37% of disposable income. Empty when Statistics Canada did not publish a figure (status ..). Official values were not altered.
Statistics Canada status symbol. .. means not available for that reference period and value is empty. Empty status means a regular published value.
Additional Statistics Canada symbol when present. Empty in all three files in this snapshot.
t if Statistics Canada has terminated this series, otherwise empty. Empty in all three files in this snapshot.
Number of decimal places Statistics Canada uses when displaying the value.

Item as published, for example Household income, Disposable income, Total debt payments, Mortgage interest paid, Total obligated payments of principal and Debt service ratio. Lines starting Plus, Equals or Of which are parts of the build up shown in the official table. Two labels, Disposable income and Of which: consumer debt, carry a trailing space in the official file and are kept exactly as published.

household_wealth_distribution.csv only. Household group as published: All households; income quintiles (based on equivalized household disposable income); wealth quintiles (based on net worth); age group of the major income earner; one person or multiple person households; main source of household income; housing tenure (owner, owner with mortgage, owner without mortgage, renter); generation; and income quintile by age group crossings.

household_wealth_distribution.csv only. Balance sheet item as published: Total assets, Financial assets, Life insurance and pensions, Other financial assets, Non-financial assets, Real estate, Other non-financial assets, Total liabilities, Mortgage liabilities, Other liabilities, and Net worth (wealth). Items are nested, so add only items at the same level.

household_wealth_distribution.csv only. Value is the total for the group in millions of dollars. Distribution of value is the group's share of the all households total for that item, in percent. Value per household is the average per household in the group, in dollars.
